newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senators propose welfare 'safety net'.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senators propose welfare 'safety net'.

text.p: A group of Democratic state Senators on Thursday proposed using savings under California Gov. Pete Wilson's welfare plan to provide a "safety net" for women, children and the elderly.
The Senators said the projected $562 million of savings over two years under Wilson's controversial welfare reform plan should be used for child care and other programs.
"I am concerned about the lack of a safety net for those that are not able to work," state Senator Hilda Solis said.

Solis proposed an income tax credit for low income wage earners along with measures allowing students enrolled in college and women escaping domestic violence to continue receiving aid. Under her plan, grandparents would not be denied aid while raising their grandchildren, she said.
Solis said her measures would protect women, children and the elderly from the governor's "punitive" welfare proposals.

"I believe we have a comprehensive legislative package that is fair and not punitive which will help transition welfare recipients into full fledged contributors to California's economy as workers and taxpayers," Solis said.
Earlier this month, Wilson, a Republican, proposed a nearly $67 billion state spending plan that called for an overhaul of the state welfare system.
In line with federal law, the governor's welfare proposal would set a state lifetime limit of five years on aid, including assistance received in other states.
But under Wilson's plan, starting from 1998, able-bodied people currently on welfare may only receive aid for a total of 24 months during any 36-month period.
New recipients may only receive aid for 12 months during any 24-month period, Wilson said.
In addition, Wilson said grants would be reduced by 15 percent for most recipients after six months on assistance.
Wilson's welfare plan has drawn fire from some Democrats concerned that it was too harsh.
A Wilson spokesman on Thursday said the governor intended for a portion of the projected welfare savings to fund programs to help move welfare recipients into jobs.
